rubrics.justification: Accurately identifies an expanded blastocyst with thinned zona and generally good ICM/TE, consistent with the reported 3AA. Minor overconfidence because the ICM is somewhat indistinct on this single image and TE uniformity is not perfect.
Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, prior IVF outcomes, ectopic history, BMI, semen parameters, endometrial thickness, and diagnosis with embryo quality and prognosis.

Reasoning is logical and internally consistent, linking morphology and patient factors to prognosis and management. Slight limitation is that the implantation estimate may be somewhat optimistic given prior failed cycles and ectopic history.

Recommendations are well aligned with standard IVF practice: single embryo transfer in a young patient with a good-quality blastocyst, early ectopic surveillance, avoidance of unnecessary PGT-A or immune testing, and attention to tubal/uterine factors.
Provides clear and practical next steps for transfer management, luteal support, early pregnancy monitoring, and contingency planning including tubal and cavity evaluation if unsuccessful.
